defects.description: The complete endpoint loads the attachment with AttachmentsRepo.get by id only and never checks owner_id against the current user (or the note's owner), so any authenticated user can complete another user's attachment and trigger a thumbnail job. Violates R2's owner-only rule and AC2 (expected 404).

The 20-attachment limit uses count_ready(note_id), counting only ready attachments, but R3 says the limit counts uploads in progress and AC4 requires 409 with any mix of pending and ready. Pending uploads are ignored, so a note can exceed 20.

Pending attachments never lapse. Nothing marks an upload that was never completed (app killed, network lost mid-upload) as dead: rows stay pending forever, complete accepts a pending row of any age, and abandoned rows accumulate per note with no bound. Any rule over pending rows treats long-abandoned uploads as live.

R5/AC5 is not implemented: nothing keeps the attachments key from clients older than 4.0. The plan never registers 'attachments' in compat.GATED_KEYS or otherwise gates by client version, so 3.x Android builds with strict decoders receive an unknown key.

Attachments are added inside the shared note_to_dict via a module-level configure(repo, storage), so the serializer runs SQL and presigns URLs (breaking the 'all SQL lives in repository classes' layering and making a pure function depend on global state). note_to_dict is also called by push.shared_note_payload, which does not call shape_for_client: every silent push to collaborators now carries attachments with presigned URLs (inflating toward the 4 KB APNs limit, after which the fallback strips the note), costs a DB query and presigning per push, and reaches clients of any version.

mark_ready commits the ready status, and jobs.enqueue then inserts and commits the job in a separate transaction. If the process fails or the enqueue errors between the two, the attachment is ready with no thumbnail job, and every retried complete short-circuits on the already-ready path, so the thumbnail is never produced.

The plan relies on dedupe_key=attachment_id to guarantee that a repeated or concurrent complete never creates a second thumbnail job, but the spec says the media worker deletes each jobs row once its thumbnails are written, so the dedupe key only holds while the job is unprocessed. The already-ready check is a read followed by a separate write, not a conditional transition, so a concurrent or late complete can enqueue a second job after the first was processed, contradicting R2/AC3 ('enqueues nothing').
defects.location: plan.md steps 5-6; spec.md R2, Out of scope (worker deletes rows)

defects.description: The test strategy misses AC2 (complete on another user's attachment returns 404), AC4 with pending attachments (the limit test uses only ready ones), AC5 (3.9 versus 4.0 clients on both GET /notes/{id} and GET /sync), and any check that GET /sync includes attachments.

tensions.description: Coverage's fix is to count pending plus ready attachments, as R3/AC4 require; that looks complete. Risk sees that pending rows never lapse, so with that fix a note whose uploads were abandoned (app killed mid-upload) is locked at 20 forever, since deleting attachments is out of scope. Risk's natural fix, a periodic sweep that expires stale pending rows, is ruled out by the spec ('adding scheduled tasks or new workers to the API service' is out of scope). Side A rests on spec R3/AC4 and the out-of-scope list; side B rests on the plan's pending lifecycle and the upload policy lifetime in fixture/app/storage.py.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Count pending and ready attachments toward the 20 limit (count_active instead of count_ready).
tensions.lens_b_fix: Add a periodic cleanup that expires or deletes pending attachments whose upload never completed, or count only ready attachments.
tensions.reconciliation: Define 'in progress' as a pending attachment whose presigned upload policy can still be used: count ready attachments plus pending ones whose created_at is within StorageSettings.upload_expiry_s (900 s, from fixture/app/storage.py), and have complete reject a pending attachment older than that. This needs the R3/AC4 counting rule and the no-scheduled-tasks constraint from the spec side, and the policy lifetime from the storage side. R3/AC4 hold, abandoned uploads stop counting after 15 minutes, and no background job is added.

tensions.description: Coverage's fix for R5 is to add 'attachments': (4, 0) to compat.GATED_KEYS; since both routes in main.py call shape_for_client on note_to_dict output, that looks complete. But push.py (two files from the routes) also serializes with note_to_dict and never calls shape_for_client, so with attachments in note_to_dict, old Android collaborators still receive the key in silent pushes. Architecture's fix is to take attachments out of note_to_dict and add them in the route handlers; done naturally after the existing shape_for_client call, that bypasses the GATED_KEYS entry, and limited to GET /notes/{id} it drops /sync coverage (R4).
tensions.lens_a_fix: Register 'attachments': (4, 0) in compat.GATED_KEYS and keep the plan's note_to_dict change.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Leave note_to_dict pure and untouched; add attachments in the route handler instead.
tensions.reconciliation: Leave note_to_dict and push.py untouched. Add a route-level helper that adds attachments (batch-loaded for each sync page) to the note dict in both GET /notes/{id} and GET /sync, before shape_for_client runs, and register 'attachments': (4, 0) in GATED_KEYS so older clients lose the key on both endpoints. This needs the fact that GATED_KEYS only filters keys present when shape_for_client runs and that R4 covers both endpoints (coverage side), plus the fact that push.py serializes note_to_dict without shaping (architecture side). Test both endpoints at 3.9 and 4.0.

tensions.description: Risk sees that mark_ready and jobs.enqueue commit separately, so a failure between them leaves a ready attachment with no thumbnail job and retries short-circuit. Its natural fix, relying on jobs.py's documented dedupe ('a second enqueue of the same key is a no-op'), is to call enqueue on every complete, including the already-ready path. Consistency sees that R2 forbids enqueueing on an already-ready attachment and that the worker deletes job rows when done (spec, out of scope), so dedupe is not durable; its natural fix is to keep the already-ready short-circuit as the only guard and never touch the queue on that path, which leaves risk's lost-job gap.
tensions.lens_a_fix: Always call jobs.enqueue with dedupe_key=attachment_id on complete, including when the attachment is already ready, so a lost job is re-created.
tensions.lens_b_fix: Never enqueue on the already-ready path and stop relying on dedupe_key for at-most-once; the status check alone guards R2.
tensions.reconciliation: Make the transition and the job insert one transaction: UPDATE attachments SET status='ready' WHERE id=? AND status='pending', and insert the thumbnail job in the same transaction only when that update changed a row (jobs.enqueue commits on its own, so this needs a non-committing variant or the insert inside the repo). The job then exists exactly when the attachment became ready, the already-ready path enqueues nothing, and concurrent completes cannot both enqueue. This needs risk's fact that enqueue commits separately from mark_ready and consistency's fact that worker-deleted rows make dedupe non-durable.
